skill.name: bigquery
skill.description: Guides cautious BigQuery CLI use for schema inspection, table discovery, row counts, metadata review, and limited sampling in Monzo projects.
skill.summary: Inspect BigQuery structures with explicit projects, Standard SQL, and data-sensitivity safeguards.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: All 81 Ruby or shell backtick alerts are false positives caused by Markdown and BigQuery identifier syntax, and both reconnaissance alerts are benign guidance. Two fixed /tmp writes remain confirmed, while semantic review found overbroad metadata authorization and disclosure of organization-specific cloud identifiers.

remediation.issue: Schema exports use the predictable shared path /tmp/columns.txt.
remediation.suggestion: Use a securely created temporary file or a user-approved destination, and prevent overwriting existing files or following symbolic links.

remediation.issue: Sensitive metadata and row-count queries are described as always allowed.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation, permission checks, sensitivity review, and cost estimation before querying any organization dataset, including metadata views.

remediation.issue: The public guide contains organization-specific project, dataset, and table identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Replace internal identifiers with neutral placeholders and keep organization-specific mappings in access-controlled documentation.

content.user_title: Inspect BigQuery Schemas with the bq CLI
content.value_statement: BigQuery exploration can expose sensitive data or consume excessive resources. This skill provides cautious bq patterns for schema inspection, table discovery, row counts, and cost checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates bq query patterns for column, table, and schema inspection through INFORMATION_SCHEMA.
Shows row-count checks that avoid returning table contents.
Lists tables and searches names with configurable project, dataset, and pattern placeholders.
Explains CSV, JSON, quiet, and row-limit output options.
Supports cautious table sampling, dry runs, and dbt source validation workflows.
limitations: Requires an installed, authenticated bq CLI and sufficient Google Cloud permissions.
Includes Monzo-specific examples that must be replaced for other organizations.
Cannot guarantee query cost, data classification, or authorization decisions.
Sampling guidance must not be used for sensitive tables without explicit approval.

use_cases.title: Inspect source schemas
use_cases.description: Review column names and types before creating or updating dbt source models.

use_cases.title: Discover warehouse tables
use_cases.description: Find relevant tables by name while avoiding access to stored row content.

use_cases.title: Investigate pipeline failures
use_cases.description: Verify source existence, schema changes, and table size before deeper debugging.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a table schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to inspect columns and types for [PROJECT].[DATASET].[TABLE] using Standard SQL. Do not query table rows.

prompt_templates.title: Find matching tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bq command that lists tables in [PROJECT].[DATASET] matching [PATTERN]. Explain placeholders and keep the query metadata-only.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a warehouse error
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose this BigQuery or dbt error: [ERROR]. Verify table existence and schema, then suggest the least invasive next check.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a controlled investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cautious investigation for [DATA_ISSUE] in [PROJECT].[DATASET]. Include permission checks, cost estimation, metadata queries, and approval before sampling rows.

output_examples.input: Inspect the schema for the orders table without reading customer rows.
output_examples.output: A metadata-only plan identifies the required project and dataset, retrieves ordered column names and types, and avoids table content.

output_examples.input: Find tables containing payment in their names.
output_examples.output: A table-discovery response searches INFORMATION_SCHEMA, sorts matching names, and asks for the project and dataset before execution.

output_examples.input: Estimate the impact of an expensive query.
output_examples.output: A cautious response recommends a dry run, reviews bytes processed, verifies permissions, and requests approval before the full query.

best_practices: Confirm the project, dataset, permissions, and data classification before running any query.
Start with INFORMATION_SCHEMA, row counts, and dry runs before accessing table contents.
Use fully qualified identifiers, Standard SQL, explicit limits, and approved output destinations.
anti_patterns: Do not query PII, employee, credential, or financial rows without explicit authorization.
Do not treat metadata access as universally safe or free.
Do not write query results to predictable shared temporary paths.

faq.question: Does this skill install or authenticate the bq CLI?
faq.answer: No. Install Google Cloud tools and authenticate through your approved organizational process.

faq.question: Can it inspect a table without reading its rows?
faq.answer: Yes. INFORMATION_SCHEMA can return column and table metadata, subject to permissions and data-governance rules.

faq.question: Does a row count expose no sensitive information?
faq.answer: Not always. Counts can reveal business activity or population size, so confirm authorization before querying.

faq.question: Can I use the Monzo project names elsewhere?
faq.answer: No. Replace organization-specific identifiers with projects and datasets that you are authorized to access.

faq.question: How can I reduce query cost risk?
faq.answer: Use dry runs, inspect table size, restrict selected columns, apply filters, and review estimated bytes before execution.

faq.question: Can this skill safely sample production data?
faq.answer: Only after confirming data classification, access permission, business purpose, output handling, and explicit user approval.
